notes: No breadboard or jumper wires are used. The battery holder leads and the motor leads go directly into the shield's screw terminals.
Channel A is the A+/A- terminal pair, mapped to shield ports OUT1 (A+) and OUT2 (A-). The orange motor wire goes to A+ and the black wire to A-, so motor + goes to OUT1 and motor - to OUT2.
The external supply goes to the VIN and GND screw terminals, mapped to VIN_T and GND_T. VIN takes the orange wire and GND the black wire.
The two 18650 cells are assumed to be in series. bat1 + is joined to bat2 -, bat2 + goes to VIN and bat1 - goes to GND. The image doesn't show how the two cells are joined inside the holder.

Mounting the shield on the Uno joins each header pin to the Uno pin with the same name. Shield GND_D is assumed to sit over Uno GND.3, by the pin-13 header. Shield GND_1 and GND_2 are matched to Uno GND.1 and GND.2.
The USB cable has no ports in the catalogue, so its edge has null ports. It runs from the Uno to the computer, which is not modelled.
Arduino pin use (D12 direction, D3 PWM, D9 brake for channel A) is software only and adds no extra physical connections.
